$comment: Among the stars and beyond (src/ui/explore/neighbourhood-panel.ts): loaded with its chunk (I18n.extend). The scene’s labels and the navigator’s entry are in en.explore.json.
ui.universe.stars.title: Among the stars
ui.universe.stars.intro: Each star where its Hipparcos parallax puts it, as bright and in the colour it would look from here. Drag to turn round, scroll to move in or out, and double-click a star to fly to it.
ui.universe.stars.where: Here: {ly} light years ({pc} pc) from the Sun
ui.universe.stars.planets: {count, plural, one {# known planet} other {# known planets}}
ui.universe.stars.planetsNote: From the NASA Exoplanet Archive. Values it calculated rather than measured are marked. Orbits are drawn face-on to the Sun, tilted by their inclination where it is measured; where each planet is on its orbit, and its size, are illustrative.
ui.universe.stars.planet.temperature: about {k} K if it absorbed all its light evenly
ui.universe.stars.search: Find a star (a name, or HIP or HR and a number)
ui.universe.stars.nearWithPlanets: {pc} pc away, {count, plural, one {# planet} other {# planets}}
ui.universe.stars.fromSunWithPlanets: {pc} pc from the Sun, {count, plural, one {# planet} other {# planets}}
ui.universe.stars.unplaced: its distance not known well enough to place it
ui.universe.stars.credit: Places: ESA’s Hipparcos (the 2007 new reduction, van Leeuwen); names: the IAU’s; planets: the NASA Exoplanet Archive. The galaxy’s band is illustrative. Beyond: the Milky Way a model (Reid et al. 2019; Bland-Hawthorn and Gerhard 2016); the Local Group, McConnachie (2012) and SIMBAD (CDS); galaxies, the Sloan Digital Sky Survey.
ui.universe.stars.whereFar: Here: {ly} light years ({pc}) from the Sun
ui.universe.stars.group.rest: neither: the Local Group itself, or near it
ui.universe.stars.beyond.title: Beyond the stars
ui.universe.stars.beyond.intro: Scroll out past the stars to the Milky Way, the galaxies around it and the web of galaxies a survey has mapped, or go to:
ui.universe.stars.beyond.view.web: the galaxies a survey has mapped
ui.universe.stars.beyond.scale.galaxy: The Milky Way here is a model, not a picture: its arms where the parallaxes of star-forming regions trace them (Reid et al. 2019), continued more faintly beyond; its disc and bar at their measured sizes (Bland-Hawthorn and Gerhard 2016). Its stars are not individually known.
ui.universe.stars.beyond.scale.local-gro: The galaxies of the Local Group where McConnachie’s catalogue (2012) puts them, each a glow its own size and brightness; the four largest as discs of points at their measured sizes and tilts (which side of each is nearer is not known). The Milky Way is the model.
ui.universe.stars.beyond.scale.universe: Each point a galaxy the Sloan Digital Sky Survey measured ({count} drawn), placed by its redshift (Planck 2018’s cosmology). The survey covers part of the sky and takes fewer galaxies farther out: the outline is the survey’s, the filaments and voids the universe’s.
ui.universe.stars.hr.title: The stars by colour and brightness
ui.universe.stars.hr.label: A Hertzsprung–Russell diagram: {count} stars by colour and brightness from 10 parsecs, the Sun circled{marked}.
ui.universe.stars.hr.caption: A Hertzsprung–Russell diagram of {count} stars placed in space, each by its colour and its brightness from 10 parsecs (Hipparcos). Most lie along the main sequence, fusing hydrogen in their cores; the giants have left it and swollen; white dwarfs are cores left behind. The Sun is circled, the star in view ringed.
ui.universe.stars.hr.captionOff: A Hertzsprung–Russell diagram of {count} stars placed in space, each by its colour and its brightness from 10 parsecs (Hipparcos). {name} is not on it: its colour, or its distance, is not known well enough.
ui.universe.stars.lightV: Its light in V, the Sun’s as 1
ui.universe.stars.luminosity: All its light, the Sun’s as 1
ui.universe.stars.archiveStar: Radius, mass and light as the NASA Exoplanet Archive gives them for a planet’s star.
